content: As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to combat infections you previously had, which could result in the reappearance of disease symptoms. Additionally, if your immune system becomes overactive, you may experience symptoms. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. While taking this medication, changes in body fat distribution may occur. These changes can include increased fat in areas such as the upper back and abdomen, and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The exact cause and long-term effects of these changes remain unknown. Fosamprenavir commonly causes a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the United States, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, contact your doctor for similar guidance. Precautions: Before taking fosamprenavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to amprenavir, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as propylene glycol in the suspension, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. Fosamprenavir may increase cholesterol and triglyceride levels in your blood, which can also be elevated due to HIV infection. This could raise your risk of heart problems, such as a heart attack. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor, as well as strategies to reduce your risk of heart disease. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and fosamprenavir may be part of that treatment. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect the removal of fosamprenavir from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide, etravirine, and rifampin. Fosamprenavir may also affect the removal of other medications from your body, impacting their effectiveness. Additionally, this medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. Lab Tests: Regular medical and laboratory tests, such as viral load, T-cell counts, liver function, cholesterol/triglyceride levels, and blood sugar levels, should be conducted while taking this medication. Missed Dose: It is crucial not to miss doses of this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is more than four hours after the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store the tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. The suspension can be stored at room temperature or in the refrigerator. Refrigeration may improve the taste of the suspension. Do not freeze the medication or store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
